summary.name: Naming names in incident writeups
summary.one_liner: A blog post arguing that incident writeups should name the engineers involved, responding to a view by Alex Hidalgo of Nobl9 that favors anonymity.
use_cases: Deciding whether to name engineers in incident reports
Understanding the second victim phenomenon in on-call work
Framing incident writeups from the individual's perspective
summary.what_it_does: The post responds to Alex Hidalgo's view that incident reports should explicitly name everyone involved, while the author usually writes reports anonymously. It explains the case for anonymity: engineers feel guilt and shame after contributing to incidents, and naming them may worsen the second victim effect. The author argues that anonymity signals that names are hidden to protect the guilty, and that naming people helps normalize the idea that incidents are system problems. The author recommends writing reports from the perspective of the people involved to show their actions were reasonable at the time and to make the writeup less normative. The post is an opinion essay, not a software tool.
notable: Contrasts two practitioners' approaches to naming people in incident reports
Draws on the safety literature's second victim phenomenon
Recommends writing incident reports from the involved person's perspective
caveats: Opinion piece; it does not present a settled best practice
Describes the author's own approach, which may not suit every organization
